messages:
incident-bot: PAGE eng-oncall @Dana L — P1: inference-prod GPU pool 'gpool-6' queue depth spiked >1200, error rate rising, customer-facing latency >5s :rotating_light:
Dana L: acked — looking. grabbing dashboards and logs now. tagging @Jessica H for infra assist.
Jessica H: on it, standing up to check GPU pool and HPA signals. pulling autoscaler events.
Dana L: initial glance: queue depth climbed over 800 at 16:12 UTC, CPU targets stayed low, but GPU utilization is pegged at 98% on gpool-6. requests are piling — some requests timed out after 30s.
Vikash: adding timeline note: we saw a deploy to model-embed-v2 at 16:05 which increased memory footprint per replica. Could be warmup + memory pressure.
Mike P: observability shows HPA attempted scale at 16:14 but no new replicas became Ready until 16:17 — pods stuck in ContainerCreating due to model load time ~90-120s.
Dana L: mitigation idea 1: temporarily route new traffic to gpool-4 (less loaded) and set fallback to smaller model-quant1 for non-critical tenants. Can we flip routing? @infra-bot?
infra-bot: routing change command queued by Jessica H: `/route set inference-prod prefer-pool gpool-4 for 10m` — will apply after safety checks.
Jessica H: applied routing change at 16:20 UTC. Confirmed new requests show up in gpool-4. Latency dropped to ~650ms for new requests. Legacy backlog still draining in gpool-6.
Dana L: mitigation idea 2: manual scale out — bump dedicated GPU pool size by +2 while we investigate HPA config. @oncall-rotation please confirm budget/permission?
oncall-rotation: confirmed emergency scale approved. Jessica H executed `scale gpool-6 --replicas +2` at 16:23 UTC. New pods scheduled.
Mike P: logs from the pods that failed to become Ready:
```
Warning  FailedScheduling  10s (x3 over 1m)  kube-scheduler  0/10 nodes are available: 10 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
ContainerCreating  Created container but failed to start init: model-loader timed out after 2m
ERROR model-loader  warmup failed for model-embed-v2: OOM while allocating 3.8GiB
```
Jessica H: hypothesis list (will update):
- H1: HPA metric configured on CPU and custom queue depth not wired — autoscaler didn't react in time to GPU pressure.
- H2: Recent model deploy increased GPU memory per replica causing fewer pods to fit on nodes -> scheduling failures.
- H3: Model warmup time (90-120s) results in long Ready latency causing burst queuing before new capacity becomes serving.
Dana L: evidence: HPA events show scaleDesired went from 8->12 at 16:14 but scaleObserved remained 8 until 16:23 due to Scheduling failures and ContainerCreating delays.
Vikash: additional evidence: node-level allocatable GPU left decreased after 16:05 deploy; some nodes show fragmentation — enough aggregate GPUs but not contiguous per pod request size.
Mike P: immediate next steps logged in-thread:
- [16:26] Jessica H: decreased per-pod gpu_request from 1 -> 0.9 for model-embed-v2 to allow bin-packing across nodes (temp).
- [16:28] Dana L: enabled queue-priority-throttling to limit non-SLAs to slow path.
- [16:30] infra-bot: Canary routing for premium customers enforced, fallback model enabled for developer-tier by config change.
Dana L: customer impact note: ~4 tenants saw 10-30% increased 5xx for a 12-minute window; SLA alerts fired for 2 customers on Dedicated plans. Incident response team alerted sales/CS.
Jessica H: collecting logs and kubectl outputs; pushing to /artifacts/incidents/1748001234/ for RCA.
Mike P: adding planned RCA agenda in thread: timeline, autoscaler metrics (HPA events, custom metrics), scheduler events, node fragmentation, model memory profile, warmup profile, routing logic.
Dana L: tagging hypotheses to validate during RCA: H1 (autoscaler metric mismatch) — assign to Mike P; H2 (deploy memory increase/scheduling) — assign to Jessica H; H3 (warmup) — assign to Vikash.
Vikash: quick repro notes: ran a local load test with 200 qps to model-embed-v2 on a 8-node cluster; observed median Ready latency 95s and 99th 130s; queue depth rose linearly and HPA didn't prevent SLO miss. Repro artifacts in artifact path.
Dana L: mitigation summary (in incident): routing to gpool-4 + manual scale added capacity; per-pod request tweak allowed schedulability; fallback models limited customer impact.
Jessica H: current status at 16:45 UTC: queue depth back to nominal (<50), gpool-6 GPUs at ~75% after scale, new nodes still warming. Will leave routing pref to gpool-4 for 15m to ensure backlog drained.
Dana L: preparing post-incident follow-up: create postmortem, list corrective actions: (a) update autoscaler to use GPU-util and queue-depth metric, (b) add pre-deploy check for model memory delta, (c) implement fast-warmup strategy (gradual load, lazy init), (d) enable bin-packing friendly resource requests, (e) SL rollback automation for heavy deploys.
Mike P: creating ticket RF-1328 for autoscaler metric change and RF-1329 for warmup library improvements.
Dana L: handoff to oncall-rotation for night monitoring: leave watch for 2h and escalate if queue depth >200.
oncall-rotation: ack — taking watch.
Dana L: thanks everyone — marking incident as mitigated, keeping thread open for RCA notes and timeline edits. :white_check_mark:
